metadata.title: Is the cost of AI catching up to markets?

content.text:
StockBrokers.com Director of Investor Research Jessica Inskip joins Jared Blikre on Market Domination to discuss the AI trade, market leadership, and where she sees opportunities for investors.
We have to be cognizant of where the runup has been. So the runup has been from technology and those AI sectors as you said, but if we look at the broader weight or the broader index, it actually ran up about 8% whereas the equal weight has ran up about 2%. And when I say that runup, I'm meaning from its previous highs prior to the Iran conflict. because the market cap weighted ran up more, it has more room to fall. So there is this cushion if you will, where it has a lower level of support. So it's actually quite healthy that we're retracting, but what I see is the technology sector as well as the industrial sector is actually in a bullish trading cycle and looks really, really good if we compare the sectors across the board.
Yeah, so I mentioned industrials before. If we have time, we'll get to that. But I want to show you the Wi-Fi interactive here. This is semiconductors. This is what's happening today, and there's a lot of red on this screen. And uh we had big blowout earnings from Micron the other day.
Mhm.
Let me just pull up that chart. I'm going to show you the year to date. That was three years. And you can see uh we got to a new high. We have come back down, but this long-term trend line since those March 30 lows, very much intact. Uh you can see it's up 300% this year. But Tuesday, we did have uh some scary news out of Korea. uh it looked like uh SK Hex was kind of rotating out of high bandwidth memory into DRAM and it just took the wind out of the sails. To me, even though the thing snapped back the next day, let me just put a five-day view here. Uh and it's not looking a lot better. It just shows you this is a very highly sensitive tape. That's what happens when you're so stretched. So what happens from here?
Yeah, I agree with you. It's the leverage. It's so interesting how leveraged it is over there in our our friends over in APAC and that we have to think about the market mechanics that I love to talk to you about Jared, as we know we go down those rabbit holes. Um but because of that leverage, I think it's bled over into the overnight futures into our markets and then we tend to recover by the end of the day, but I still think it's a healthy backdrop. So, it is interesting, it's a finance picture because we're seeing this astronomical growth that is coming from memory. Like you said with Micron, the margins are incredible from that earnings report.
86% gross margin that they're looking for next year. I it might be, I don't know, 85, 87%, it's huge.
Yeah, and that so that pricing power and the people who are paying that bill are the magnificent seven.
